newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong puts damper on smuggled firecrackers.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong puts damper on smuggled firecrackers.

text.p: Revellers wanting to make Hong Kong's return to Chinese rule go with a bang had their hopes doused on Friday when customs officers announced their largest ever haul of smuggled firecrackers.

Authorities seized over 10 tonnes of China-made firecrackers and other fireworks and arrested the driver of a container truck, said Kwok Sin-chik, divisional customs chief at Lok Ma Chau, on Hong Kong's land border with China.
The 667 boxes of firecrackers were found on Thursday hidden behind crates of rattan chairs, Kwok told Reuters.
"Our officers became suspicious when they saw (the truck) weighed so much when it was supposed to be carrying only rattan chairs," he added.
Firecrackers are strictly banned in Hong Kong for safety reasons. People are often caught smuggling in small quantities.

Kwok declined to speculate on whether the haul was linked to handover parties. Hong Kong reverts to China at midnight on June 30, and people all over the territory are gearing up for lavish celebrations.
